title: A Fairer Meeting Schedule
script: Sari: [warmly] Daniel, can we review the time of our weekly team meeting?
Daniel: Is Wednesday at eight no longer working for you?
Sari: [honestly] I can attend, but I take my mother to a clinic twice a month. I have missed important decisions.
Daniel: I did not know that. Two remote teammates also join very late in their time zone.
Sari: [thoughtful] Could we choose a time that shares the difficulty more fairly?
Daniel: Yes. Let us check everyone's working hours instead of guessing.
Sari: [carefully] I made a table. Tuesday at ten works for six people, but one teammate teaches a client class then.
Daniel: What about Thursday at two?
Sari: [reflective] That works for everyone except me once a month, and I can move that appointment.
Daniel: It sounds better than making the same people struggle every week.
Sari: [practically] Agreed. We should also ask whether every topic needs a live meeting.
Daniel: The project updates could be written before Thursday. Then meeting time can focus on decisions and questions.
Sari: [calmly] That may reduce the meeting from sixty minutes to thirty-five.
Daniel: Shorter meetings would help the teammate joining near the end of her day.
Sari: [encouraging] How will we make sure absent people are not forgotten?
Daniel: We can record decisions in the shared note, with an owner and deadline for each action.
Sari: Let us propose Thursday at two for a one-month trial and invite comments privately too.
Daniel: [warmly] Why privately?
Sari: Some people may hesitate to discuss care duties or personal schedules in a large group.
Daniel: Good point. Fair planning needs information, but people should control what they share.
Sari: [pleasantly] I will send the proposal today. After four meetings, we will review attendance and make another adjustment if needed.

quiz.question: Why does Sari miss some Wednesday meetings?
options: She takes her mother to a clinic
quiz.explanation: A regular care duty conflicts twice a month.

quiz.question: Who else has difficulty?
options: Remote teammates in a late time zone
quiz.explanation: The fixed time also affects distant colleagues.

quiz.question: What time do they propose?
quiz.explanation: Thursday at two is the most workable option.

quiz.question: How may they shorten meetings?
options: Write updates first and discuss decisions live

quiz.question: Why invite private comments?
options: People may not want to reveal personal duties publicly
quiz.explanation: Privacy can support fair schedule planning.

quiz.question: What personal duty affects Sari?
options: Taking a parent to an appointment

quiz.question: Who else struggles with the time?
options: A colleague in another time zone
quiz.explanation: The issue affects more than one person.

quiz.question: What may replace some live topics?
quiz.explanation: Not every item needs real-time discussion.

quiz.question: Why allow private comments?
quiz.explanation: People may not want to explain needs publicly.

quiz.question: What follows four trial meetings?
quiz.explanation: The schedule remains testable and responsive.
